functions.signature: void bwapi_abi_version(int32_t* major, int32_t* minor, int32_t* patch)
functions.doc: The ABI's own version, written to the three out-params; any of them may be NULL and is then skipped. 0.x is explicitly unstable; append-only begins at 1.0, the exit of the consumers phase. Three int32_t out-params rather than a packed word, so there is nothing to document about packing.
The ABI's own version as "major.minor.patch".
BWAPI::CLIENT_VERSION of the pinned BWAPI (10003 today). The server refuses a client whose version differs from its own, so a host can check compatibility before connecting.
SVN_REV of the pinned BWAPI, from upstream's own revision generator (plan section 10.3).
1 when the pinned BWAPI was built with BUILD_DEBUG, 0 otherwise.

The BWAPI_ERR_* code latched by the first failing call since the last bwapi_clear_last_error(), or BWAPI_ERR_NONE. Sticky: successful calls do not touch it and reading does not clear it. Clear it at the top of the frame and check it before bwapi_client_update(). This is a different lifetime from BWAPI's own Game::getLastError(), which is per call and comes back through bwapi_game_get_last_error().
The message that came with the latched code: a BWEM::Exception's what(), the two unit ids of an overlap, the name of the export a bad handle was passed to. Empty when nothing is latched.
Resets the sticky error channel to BWAPI_ERR_NONE and clears its message.

Installs where the ABI's own diagnostics go, at BWAPI_LOG_* levels, with the user pointer handed back on every call. NULL disables. Client::connect() still writes to std::cout and std::cerr itself in this version.

Installs a callback invoked at the moment an error is latched, with the code, its message and the user pointer, so a wrapper can raise at the failing call rather than poll. Off by default; NULL disables. The sticky latch is unchanged either way. The callback runs with the re-entrancy depth raised, so a mutating call from inside it is rejected with BWAPI_ERR_REENTRANT_MUTATION once that guard is emitted.

Connects to a running BWAPI server over its shared memory and pipe. Returns 1 on success and 0 when no server is up, in which case retry after a pause. Records the calling thread as the thread every later call must come from. Already connected: latches BWAPI_ERR_ALREADY_CONNECTED and returns 0.

Ends the frame and BLOCKS on the pipe until the server hands back the next one. Every event index and snapshot from the previous frame is invalid afterwards. If the server has gone away, bwapi_client_is_connected() is 0 on return.
Tears down BWEM first, because its map points into the game data, then the client. Safe to call when not connected.
1 while connected. Becomes 0 when the server goes away during bwapi_client_update().
The player's id, which is the handle itself: 0..11, the slot in the game's player table.

functions.signature: int32_t bwapi_player_get_name(bwapi_player_id player_id, char* buf, int32_t buf_len)
functions.doc: The player's name, as the game reports it.

functions.signature: int32_t bwapi_player_get_units(bwapi_player_id player_id, int32_t* out, int32_t cap)
functions.doc: The ids of every unit the player owns, incomplete units included, ascending. Units loaded into transports, bunkers, refineries, assimilators or extractors are not included, as in BWAPI.
The player's race. BWAPI_RACE_UNKNOWN when the player chose Random and the race has not been revealed to this bot.
The player's controller type, a BWAPI_PLAYERTYPE_* value. Other bots are reported as human players, as BWAPI reports them.
The id of the force (team) the player belongs to.
1 when the player is allied with the other player. 0 when not, and also when either player is neutral or an observer.
1 when the player is at war with the other player. 0 when not, and also when either player is neutral or an observer.
1 when this is the neutral player, which owns the minerals, geysers and critters.
The player's starting location in tile coordinates. BWAPI_TILEPOSITION_NONE when the player has no start location, BWAPI_TILEPOSITION_UNKNOWN when BWAPI could not retrieve it.
1 when the player has achieved victory.
1 when the player has been defeated.
1 when the player has left the game.
The player's current minerals. 0 when the player's information is inaccessible to this bot.
The player's current vespene gas. 0 when the player's information is inaccessible to this bot.
The minerals the player has gathered since the game began, starting minerals included. 0 when inaccessible.
The vespene gas the player has gathered since the game began, starting gas included. 0 when inaccessible.
The minerals the player has spent on repairs since the game began. 0 when inaccessible.
The vespene gas the player has spent on repairs since the game began. 0 when inaccessible.
The minerals the player has recovered by cancelling units and structures. 0 when inaccessible.
The vespene gas the player has recovered by cancelling units and structures. 0 when inaccessible.
The minerals the player has spent, repairs excluded. 0 when inaccessible.
The vespene gas the player has spent, repairs excluded. 0 when inaccessible.
The supply available to the player for the given race, or for the player's own race when race is BWAPI_RACE_NONE. Supply is per race, and the value is double what the game displays, as in BWAPI.
The supply the player is using for the given race, or for the player's own race when race is BWAPI_RACE_NONE. Double what the game displays, as in BWAPI.
How many units of the type the player has, incomplete ones included; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type. In-progress Zerg units count as their egg type until they hatch.
How many units of the type the player has that are strictly visible to this bot, even when information on the player is unrestricted; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.
How many completed units of the type the player has; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.
How many incomplete units of the type the player has, which is the all count less the completed count; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type. Zerg units inside eggs are not counted.
How many of the player's units of the type have died; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.
How many units of the type the player has killed; BWAPI_UNIT_ALL_UNITS counts every type.
The level the player has attained for the upgrade, 0 when none.
1 when the player has researched the technology.
1 while the player is researching the technology.
1 while the player is upgrading the upgrade.

returns.neutral: 255, the Unknown id of Color, which has no named Unknown

functions.doc: The player's colour as a palette index, the value the drawing functions take.
The control character that switches text to the player's colour, as a BWAPI_TEXT_* value; put it in a string passed to the drawing and text functions.
The maximum energy a unit of the type has for this player, the player's energy upgrades included.
The top speed of a unit of the type for this player, the player's speed upgrades included.
The maximum range of the weapon for this player, the player's range upgrades included.
The sight range of a unit of the type for this player, the player's sight upgrades included.
The ground weapon cooldown of a unit of the type for this player, the player's attack speed upgrades included.
The armour a unit of the type has for this player, upgrades included.
The damage the weapon deals for this player, upgrades included.
The player's unit score, as on the end-game score screen.
The player's kill score, as on the end-game score screen.
The player's building score, as on the end-game score screen.
The player's razing score, as on the end-game score screen.
The player's custom score, which map triggers set.
1 when the player is an observer, typically in a use-map-settings observer game.
The highest level of the upgrade available to this player, which map settings may lower from the type's own maximum.
1 when the player is allowed to research the technology under the map's settings.
1 when the player is allowed to create units of the type under the map's settings.

functions.signature: int32_t bwapi_player_has_unit_type_requirement(bwapi_player_id player_id, int32_t unit_type, int32_t amount)
functions.doc: 1 when the player has at least amount completed units of the type, counting the equivalents BWAPI counts: a Lair or Hive for a Hatchery, a Hive for a Lair, a sieged tank for an unsieged one, and both Templar and Archon forms. Pass 1 for the plain requirement.

constants.doc: The ABI's own error codes, latched by the sticky first-error channel. A code says which section-4 rule fired. None of these values is ever reused.

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_NONE
values.doc: nothing latched since the last clear

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_WRONG_THREAD
values.doc: a call from a thread other than the update thread

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_REENTRANT_MUTATION
values.doc: a mutating call from inside a callback

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_BWEM
values.doc: a BWEM::Exception, or a map BWEM would crash on

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_INVALID_HANDLE
values.doc: an id that could never have been valid

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED
values.doc: a game or unit call before connect, or after disconnect

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_BAD_BUFFER
values.doc: a NULL buffer with a nonzero cap or buf_len, or a negative one

values.name: BWAPI_ERR_EXCEPTION
values.doc: a C++ exception other than BWEM's escaped the wrapped call; what() is the message

constants.doc: The level argument of the log callback. Client::connect()'s own std::cout and std::cerr output is not redirected in v1; these carry the ABI's diagnostics.

values.name: BWAPI_LOG_WARN
values.doc: a rejected re-entrant call, among others

constants.doc: BWAPI's own position sentinels (BWAPI/Position.h) in unpacked form, for the pixel, walk (scale 8) and tile (scale 32) scales. The packed forms are BWAPI_POS_MAKE of each pair; packing is lossless, so a C++ bot sees the same values. BWAPI_POSITION_NONE packed is the neutral return of every position-returning function.
